title: A Thorn for the Garden
premise: Hazel Reyes has hidden her gift behind harmless charms for three years, guarding a sealed gate in the city of Vell that binds an ancient hunger beneath the earth. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive and the gate begins to fail, she learns the 'king' who outlawed magic is no longer human—a usurper wearing the dead king's face, sustained by the very power he forbids. Hazel must gather outcast magicians, thieves, and one disillusioned hunter to unbind the false king before his armies crush the free cities. In the end she reopens the gate at terrible cost, feeding the thing below the usurper's stolen magic—and sacrificing her own gift—to seal it forever, choosing to become ordinary in a world that finally needs magic.
about_author: Cyrus Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forbidden grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who survive by hiding, and what happens when hiding stops working.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: Hazel Reyes sells luck-knots and fever-charms in Vell's night market, keeping her true gift buried. POV: Hazel. She feels the sealed gate tremble beneath her shop and quietly reinforces it, establishing her secret duty. Emotional beat: weary vigilance—the cost of invisibility.

chapters.title: The King's Edict
chapters.summary: Crown criers announce a realm-wide hunt for anyone with the gift; neighbor turns on neighbor. POV: Hazel, with a brief interlude from hunter Captain Dain Marrow. A charm-buyer is dragged away screaming while Hazel does nothing. Emotional beat: guilt and fear—survival demands complicity.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Hazel witnesses the king at a public rite and senses nothing human inside him—only borrowed magic stitched over a hollow. POV: Hazel. She realizes the edict isn't persecution but harvest, flushing out gifted blood to feed the thing on the throne. Emotional beat: horrified clarity.

chapters.title: The Gatekeeper's Burden
chapters.summary: Hazel seeks her late mentor's records and learns the gate was built to imprison a devourer—and that every keeper dies young holding it shut. The gate is failing faster now, starved of magic. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: dread; her hiding place was always a death sentence deferred.

chapters.title: Outcasts
chapters.summary: Hazel flees Vell and finds the smuggler city of Brask, where hunted magicians hide: a hedge-witch, a storm-touched child, and Sera, a thief who once stole from Hazel. POV: Hazel with Sera scenes. They form a fragile alliance. Emotional beat: cautious belonging among the condemned.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Doubt
chapters.summary: Captain Dain Marrow, ordered to burn Brask, discovers the 'evidence' against its residents is fabricated by the crown itself. He defects, bringing maps of the palace's deep vaults. POV: Dain. Emotional beat: shattered faith—justice cannot live inside the law he served.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Name
chapters.summary: In the palace archives, the group learns the usurper is the dead queen's brother, who bound himself to the devourer's magic to seize the throne—and that only the gate's original binding can unmake him. POV: alternating Hazel and Dain. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Armies at the Wall
chapters.summary: The usurper's legions reach the free cities; Brask burns as the allies escape through Hazel's old gate tunnels. The storm-child is lost covering their retreat. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into fury—the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Hazel infiltrates the throne room during the coronation feast and confronts the usurper, peeling away his stolen face while Dain holds off the guard. She drags him bodily to the failing gate and feeds him to the devourer below. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: climax—terror, rage, and terrible necessity.

chapters.title: A Thorn for the Garden
chapters.summary: To reseal the gate, Hazel pours her own gift into the binding, becoming the first keeper to survive—ordinary, magicless, alive. The free cities rebuild; magic returns lawless and free. POV: Hazel, closing with Sera. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace—identity found not in power, but in choice.
